item: Row 423: the post-import analysis drain goes newest article first, and resumes from the analysis stamps
summary: The drain after an import analysed a batch in article id order (merge insertion order), so on a large import the recent news a reader looks at first was analysed last. reindex_imported_articles now reads the batch once, ordered published_at IS NULL, published_at DESC, id DESC (a LEFT JOIN, so an id naming no article any more stays in the list and is counted out as before). The id watermark was an exact cursor only in ascending id order, so the resume no longer filters on it: the two analysis stamps, written by index_article in the same transaction as the rows, already said what is done, and a resume is handed exactly batch minus certified minus stand-ins (tested with a crash after half a batch, under which the old watermark would have skipped every owed article with a lower id). The cursor file stays for the progress line and the journal, its last_id diagnostic only; a failed article is retried on resume. Draining newest first writes the same mentions, keywords, places, entities, dates, sentiment and stamps as draining in id order (two copies of one corpus, keyword ids compared through term and language); keyword ids are handed out in processing order, so where an article's top keyword is a tie the representative (lowest id, documented as meaningless) can differ, and an article of unknown language still files under the lowest-id row of a term. No schema change, no version bump, no re-extraction; reindex_all_batch and backfill_corpus are unchanged.
